short_summary.value: Combinational operand bit-order transformation unit for ARM byte/bit/halfword reversal instructions
short_summary.explanation: Module has no event inputs or outputs, no sequential elements, and no instances. All 44 assignments are combinational and interface-related, transforming the 32-bit oprand input into four candidate results selected by reverseType control. This matches a pure combinational data reordering function.

responsibility_claims.value: Combinational operand bit-order transformation unit for ARM byte/bit/halfword reversal instructions
responsibility_claims.explanation: Module has no event inputs or outputs, no sequential elements, and no instances. All 44 assignments are combinational and interface-related, transforming the 32-bit oprand input into four candidate results selected by reverseType control. This matches a pure combinational data reordering function.

responsibility_claims.value: Produces bit-reversed copy of oprand (bit 0 becomes bit 31, etc.)
responsibility_claims.explanation: Assignments 0-31 directly connect each bit of w_rbitResult_32 to the opposite-indexed bit of oprand, forming a complete 32-bit bit-reversal. This is a pure wire permutation with no logic.

responsibility_claims.value: Reverses byte order of oprand (byte 0 becomes byte 3, etc.)
responsibility_claims.explanation: Assignments 32-35 swap the four byte lanes of oprand into w_revResult_32. Each 8-bit slice is directly connected to the opposite byte position.

responsibility_claims.value: Reverses byte order within each 16-bit halfword of oprand
responsibility_claims.explanation: Assignments 36-39 swap byte pairs within each halfword: upper halfword bytes are swapped, lower halfword bytes are swapped. This is REV16 semantics.

responsibility_claims.value: Reverses byte order of lower halfword and sign-extends to 32 bits
responsibility_claims.explanation: Assignment 40 extracts oprand[7:0] and sign-extends to 24 bits based on oprand[7]. Assignment 42 places oprand[15:8] into w_revshResult_32[7:0]. Assignment 41 concatenates the sign extension into upper 24 bits. This implements REVSH semantics.

documentation_focus.value: Manual should document the reverseType encoding and each reversal operation's bit-level mapping
documentation_focus.explanation: The module's entire function is defined by the reverseType encoding and the four wire permutations. Each operation (RBIT, REV, REV16, REVSH) should be documented with bit mapping diagrams showing how oprand bits map to result bits.

interpretation.value: Multiplexes four candidate reversal results based on reverseType control
interpretation.explanation: Assignment 43 selects among w_rbitResult_32 (00), w_revResult_32 (01), w_rev16Result_32 (10), and w_revshResult_32 (11) using reverseType[1:0]. Defaults to 32'b0 for undefined codes. This is the output data path mux.
